title: Sonny Greer's tempo trouble and Duke's reply, "Greer is ill. Do you know a physician?"
summary: At the Chicago Theater Greer's drinking ruined tempos behind Sarah Vaughan, and Duke deflected George Treadwell's complaint.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: I remember an experience, we were working the Chicago Theater, and they had -- we used to have to do like six shows a day, which is a hard day. We'd do the shopping show, which was about noontime, you know, into the closing hours. And I was working with Sarah Vaughan at that point, and Sonny Greer was with Duke, and well you know how Sonny would go out and have his drinks.
When he got to the theater he had his thing going, you know? And he was sitting -- if you remember how that pyramid setup that Ellington had.
Sonny was sitting up top, and they rolled a piano out for me and Duke would stand up at the little upright piano, but he was doing the conducting at that point.

And so we were playing -- we'd played, 'Perdido,' and we noticed -- all the booze had gone into Sonny's legs and the tempo was going haywire. So by this time Duke and I had become friends and George Treadwell was managing Sarah at that point, and he didn't know how to handle Duke about Sonny, because Sarah would come off of the stand crying. The arrangement was great and the band -- the horns were playing it
beautifully, but Sonny was -- had just been hanging out too much, you know?
So we went to Duke's dressing room. George told me to come and I didn't want to go because I'm in the middle there, you know?

So we walked in and Duke was sitting there and at that time he had a lot of weight. He looked like Buddha. And he asked -- Treadwell asked him, said, "Well, can't you get him to play on the high hat," which is a cymbal that would be definite, you know, keep a definite tempo or something, you know. Everybody can hear it. And he says, "Can't you get him to do that, Duke?" And Duke had the most classic answer. He says, "I don't know. Greer is ill. Do you know a physician?"

So the best we could do was just walk out of his dressing room. There was no answer to that. George Treadwell was -- he said, "Gee whiz." And Sarah was still in her dressing room, crying. He said, "Well, Greer's ill. Do you know a physician?"
He was a very unique man.
